title: Air India to Restore Daily Delhi-Dhaka Flights From July 29 as Visa Services Resume
excerpt: The carrier will return to seven weekly flights between the two capitals after cutting services in May, as India-Bangladesh bilateral ties normalise under the new BNP government.
body:
Air India will restore daily flights on the Delhi-Dhaka route from July 29, reversing capacity cuts imposed in mid-May when airspace restrictions and high jet fuel prices forced the Tata-owned carrier to scale back international operations.

Under the revised schedule, flights will depart Delhi at 11:10 a.m. and leave Dhaka for the return journey at 3:10 p.m., according to the airline's booking system. The route had been operating on just four days a week — Sundays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays — since June.

Why Services Were Cut

On May 13, Air India announced a "temporary rationalisation" of its international network for June through August, citing the conflict in West Asia that has restricted several overfly routes and pushed jet fuel prices to record highs.

Delhi-Dhaka flights were reduced from seven a week to four, while the Mumbai-Dhaka route was suspended entirely through August. The airline trimmed dozens of other routes as well, including services to San Francisco, Toronto, Paris, Melbourne, Singapore, and Shanghai, though it said it would still operate more than 1,200 international flights each month.

"We are making temporary adjustments to select international services between June and August 2026, necessitated by continued airspace restrictions over certain regions and record high jet fuel prices for international operations."

— Air India, press statement

Visa Restoration Fuels Demand

The restoration of daily flights coincides with a broader thaw in India-Bangladesh relations. On June 28, India resumed issuing tourist visas to Bangladeshi nationals from five visa application centres in Dhaka, Rajshahi, Chittagong, Sylhet, and Khulna — ending a nearly two-year freeze.

India's new High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, announced the visa resumption shortly after presenting his credentials in Dhaka. "We hope that this will further strengthen the people-to-people ties between our two sovereign nations," Trivedi said at the Indian Visa Application Centre on June 25.

Visa services had been disrupted since August 2024, when a student-led uprising toppled the government of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. During the suspension, India issued roughly 1,500 visas, mostly for medical treatment and emergencies. The number of Bangladeshi visitors to India plunged from 2.12 million in 2023 to 470,000 in 2025, according to The Business Standard.

Diplomatic Context

Relations have stabilised since Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's BNP-led government took office in February 2026, replacing the interim administration that had governed during the post-uprising period. Bangladesh has already restored all visa categories for Indian citizens, issuing more than 13,000 since February.

Technical-level talks between the two countries have resumed across trade, customs, water sharing, border management, and consular affairs. India has also transported diesel to Bangladesh to help ease energy shortages linked to the West Asia conflict.

What Remains Suspended

Air India has not announced when the Mumbai-Dhaka route will resume. That service, along with Delhi-Shanghai, Chennai-Singapore, and Delhi-Malé, remains suspended through August. The carrier said it "continues to work closely with the regulators, airport authorities, and industry partners to restore full capacity as soon as conditions permit."

The Air India Group, owned by Tata Sons, currently operates more than 300 aircraft and serves 60 domestic and 51 international destinations.

For travellers between India and Bangladesh, the return to daily Delhi-Dhaka service offers more flexible scheduling. With tourist visas now processing again and passenger demand rising, the route's full restoration signals that the worst of the India-Bangladesh travel disruption may be over.
